topics.topic: Precedence and parsing order between depth rejection, authentication, and schema validation
questions: For a request that is too deep and also has a missing, unknown or revoked token, which refusal wins, and may the kernel inspect the token before completing the depth check?
For a request that is both over-depth and missing, unknown or revoked-token, which refusal wins, and how much of the request may be parsed before authentication?

For a request that is both over the depth limit and has an unknown token or another schema error, does the depth check precede token extraction and A16's fixed order, or does A16 remain size, token, schema with depth checked during schema validation?

quotes: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null; the fit is pydantic's in JSON mode, the request model's model_validate_json over the canonical JSON text of the arguments with strict=True, since strict validation of Python objects refuses an enum given as its value string and a tuple given as a JSON array, which is how every request carries them; a ValueError the fit raises (pydantic's ValidationError is one) is raised again as InvalidRequestError, so translate_failure answers invalid_request, never internal_error — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1). initialize, ping and tools/list name no catalogue operation and are answered after the size and token checks, as the note on methods says.

answer_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Before any other bound is checked and before the arguments are walked or canonicalised, the depth of the arguments MUST be within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant — a scalar 0, an array or object one more than its deepest member, 1 when it has none —, measured without recursion, else invalid_request; a deeper request never reaches a recursive walk.
judgement.why: The later surface text fixes size and authentication before argument-depth validation, so an invalid token wins and the arguments are depth-checked only after authentication.

topics.topic: Whether internally constructed or wrapped JSON is depth-limited and what outcome applies
questions: Does `json_depth_max` also bound JSON values constructed inside the kernel, especially when wrapping an accepted depth-64 element creates a depth-65 mapped list; if so, what existing refusal or execution outcome concludes that case?

Does `json_depth_max` limit only JSON crossing into the kernel, or also every internally constructed value passed to JCS; if internal canonicalisation is limited, what outcome applies when its wrapper pushes it over the ceiling?

Does the ceiling also govern JSON values constructed inside the kernel—mapped output arrays, HTTP JSON bodies, approval request descriptions, response envelopes, and the composite meaning facts canonicalized for identities—or only JSON crossing an ingress boundary?

quotes: canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1) and is neither held exactly by an IEEE double nor written exactly as that double's ECMAScript shortest round-trip form — 100000000000000000000, which a double holds exactly, and 18014398509481990, the form JCS writes for 1.801439850948199e+16, are each that double, so canonical bytes always parse again to the same bytes —, when the value nests deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, the depth of a scalar being 0 and of an array or object one more than its deepest member, 1 when it has none, found while parsing and never by a recursion deeper than that constant, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.

translate_failure: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST map a failure to its code of = models.RefusalCode: UnknownReferenceError to unknown_reference, RefusedError to refused, InvalidRequestError and NonCanonicalValueError to invalid_request; StoreInternalError, StopRequiredError and every other exception to internal_error.
judgement.why: The later notes route internally constructed mapped lists, identity documents and request descriptions through the depth-checking canonicalizer and define the resulting exception mapping.

topics.topic: Whether service bodies not otherwise parsed as outputs must be JSON-parsed and depth-checked
questions: Must the kernel JSON-parse and depth-check non-2xx bodies and 2xx bodies for bindings without outputs, or does `json_depth_max` apply only when A09 already treats a response body as JSON output?
Which response bodies are JSON-depth checked: every body that happens to contain JSON, only a 2xx JSON body whose outputs are used, or only the selected output-member values?

Must the kernel parse JSON-looking bodies solely to enforce depth for bindings without outputs and for non-2xx answers, or does the depth rule apply only to response bodies A09 already parses as JSON outputs?

quotes: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — a request, with every value, constant and schema it submits, a service's answer, a function's output — and is checked there before any other walk of that value.

The body of an answer that is not used is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it is kept as `failure_detail` — the body decoded as UTF-8, each invalid sequence replaced by U+FFFD, then cut at a character boundary to its longest prefix that fits as UTF-8 bytes — whose class is the highest of the execution's class and the classes the binding declares for its outputs, under A07 rule 5.

Members no port names are ignored, and a binding without output ports reads the body only up to `service_response_bytes_max` — a longer one is `contract_violation` by the table of rule 5 — and does not parse or validate it.
judgement.why: A20 requires a service answer that is a JSON value to be depth-checked before any other walk, while A09 expressly forbids interpreting unused bodies and parsing or validating bodies for bindings without outputs.

topics.topic: Which roots and enclosing wrappers count when measuring request, function-output, and service-response depth
questions: Is depth measured on the complete request envelope, on each submitted value/schema independently, or on both; and does a function result or service JSON response include its enclosing output object in the measurement?
Is the limit applied to the complete MCP request document, separately to submitted argument values, constants and schemas, or both?
Is depth measured on the returned output dict, on each output-port value, or on both, and can a port value at depth exactly `json_depth_max` be accepted despite the dict wrapper?

Is depth measured on the complete request envelope, on each submitted logical value/schema/constant independently, or on both? A run input at depth 64 necessarily makes its enclosing request deeper than 64.

Is the limit applied to the returned output dictionary, to each value-port output independently, or both, especially when the dictionary also contains file-port `bytes`; and which A03 outcome records an over-depth value?

For a JSON service response, is depth measured on the whole response object or on each bound output member, and does an over-depth response conclude `contract_violation` with an `applied` attempt for a non-read 2xx response?

quotes: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — a request, with every value, constant and schema it submits, a service's answer, a function's output — and is checked there before any other walk of that value.

A request whose arguments nest deeper than `json_depth_max`, however deep, is refused `invalid_request` and the kernel answers the next request; a run input value nested exactly `json_depth_max` deep is accepted and one level deeper is refused.
judgement.why: Bounding the containing request to the same depth makes a run-input value at exactly the maximum impossible to accept because its request wrapper is necessarily deeper.

topics.topic: Outcome precedence when a function output exceeds both depth and byte limits
questions: When a function output is both deeper than `json_depth_max` and larger than `output_bytes`, is the outcome `contract_violation` for the unrepresentable value or `resource_exhausted` under A03's precedence?

When a function result is both over-depth and would exceed `output_bytes`, or cannot be canonicalised far enough to determine its byte count, is the outcome `contract_violation` or `resource_exhausted`?

quotes: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — a request, with every value, constant and schema it submits, a service's answer, a function's output — and is checked there before any other walk of that value.

The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every `value` output and the bytes of every `file` output of the one call of `run` — for a `many` file output, the sum of its elements' bytes.

Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds deciding: wall deadline passed — `timeout`; a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised — `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the process exited abnormally — `crashed`; the returned dict does not have exactly the output ports, or a value fails its port's schema, or a file output is not `bytes` — `contract_violation`; otherwise the execution succeeded.
judgement.why: A20 requires the depth rejection before any other walk, but A03 requires walking and canonicalizing the value to count bytes and gives an output-byte violation precedence over contract violation.

topics.topic: Whether grandfathered over-depth records remain exempt when reproduced or wrapped as new outputs
questions: Does grandfathering cover only direct use and return of the stored record, or also a newly produced function output, mapped aggregate or service output whose content equals or contains a grandfathered over-depth value?

After `json_depth_max` is lowered, what happens when an exempt older deep value is passed through a function or service and re-enters as an otherwise equal output: is it still exempt because the run must execute and return it as before, or rejected because every function output and service answer is a new ingress?

topics.topic: Whether manifests and installation configuration are depth-limited and how violations are reported
questions: Does `json_depth_max` apply to manifest records and installation configuration, and if so which existing refusal or start/send outcome represents an over-deep document?

Does “every JSON value” include platform-manifest files and any JSON installation configuration, which also enter the kernel but are absent from the stated list; if so, which existing refusal or startup outcome represents an over-depth document?

quotes: read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not an absolute path; it cannot be opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, each component with os.O_NOFOLLOW, whose presence is never tested, each directory on the way also with os.O_PATH and os.O_DIRECTORY and the file itself also with os.O_NONBLOCK (A17), the file so opened is not a regular file, is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name. The ownership, mode and regular-file checks and the read MUST all use that one opened file, so the file checked is the file read.

read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

read_service_record: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST project the record into ManifestServiceRecord: an instance's class becomes instance_class, its key in instances becomes instance_name, exposed_as http_api given as one string, a list or absent becomes the tuple of its routes, and each capability's record_digest is content_identity of the canonical JSON of that one raw capability entry; effect_class stays text.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1) and is neither held exactly by an IEEE double nor written exactly as that double's ECMAScript shortest round-trip form — 100000000000000000000, which a double holds exactly, and 18014398509481990, the form JCS writes for 1.801439850948199e+16, are each that double, so canonical bytes always parse again to the same bytes —, when the value nests deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, the depth of a scalar being 0 and of an array or object one more than its deepest member, 1 when it has none, found while parsing and never by a recursion deeper than that constant, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
judgement.why: The later contracts give configuration its exhaustive installation-validation path without the depth ceiling, while manifest capability entries pass through depth-limited canonicalization for their digests.

topics.topic: Whether object member names or pairs contribute to JSON depth
questions: For an object, is depth computed only from each member value, or do member names or member pairs contribute another level?
For an object, does “members” mean only member values, or do member names also participate in depth?

quotes: The depth of a JSON value is 0 for a scalar and, for an array or an object, one more than the deepest of its members, 1 when it has none; `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — a request, with every value, constant and schema it submits, a service's answer, a function's output — and is checked there before any other walk of that value.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1) and is neither held exactly by an IEEE double nor written exactly as that double's ECMAScript shortest round-trip form — 100000000000000000000, which a double holds exactly, and 18014398509481990, the form JCS writes for 1.801439850948199e+16, are each that double, so canonical bytes always parse again to the same bytes —, when the value nests deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, the depth of a scalar being 0 and of an array or object one more than its deepest member, 1 when it has none, found while parsing and never by a recursion deeper than that constant, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
judgement.divergence: One implementer measures an object's depth as one plus the maximum depth of its member values, while another treats each name/value pair or member name as an additional level; a caller submitting an object at the boundary sees acceptance from the first implementation and `invalid_request` or another depth failure from the second.
judgement.why: Neither State 2 nor the later canonicalization text defines whether an object member means only its value or whether its name or pair contributes a level.
